facts.fact: Teraco says it is a carrier-neutral colocation provider whose data centres in Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban host the NAPAfrica exchange and interconnect over 655 networks including ISPs, CDNs, cloud providers and enterprises.

ZAF.note: Nothing on a national digital strategy.

facts.fact: Teraco says NAPAfrica traffic peaked at 100 Gbps in 2016, 500 Gbps in 2018, 2 Tbps in 2021, over 4 Tbps in 2023 and 5 Tbps in February 2025.
Teraco says Akamai, Amazon, Cloudflare, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Netflix are present at NAPAfrica, and that Netflix Open Connect is hosted in Cape Town and Durban.
Teraco says NAPAfrica operates exchange points in Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban, with over 655 members from over 50 countries.
Teraco says South Africa is a landing point for the 2Africa, ACE, EASSy, Equiano, METISS, SAT3/SAFE, Seacom and WACS submarine cables.
facts.system: 2Africa, ACE, EASSy, Equiano, METISS, SAT3/SAFE, Seacom, WACS

ZAF.note: No share of people using the internet is given.

facts.fact: Teraco, the carrier-neutral colocation operator, is described as majority-owned by Digital Realty (NYSE: DLR) with a consortium of private equity investors including Berkshire Partners and Permira.
